title: Spectrum of the partially transposed Haar moment operator: eigenvalue formula for every partial transposition and the resulting rank
author: Riccardo Castellano, Dmitry Grinko, Sadra Boreiri, Nicolas Brunner, Jef Pauwels
work: Stronger Welch Bounds and Optimal Approximate $k$-Designs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Proposition 2 (source label 'prop:PT-toric-Haar-spectrum'), the spectral description of the partially transposed Haar moment operator: for every partial transposition over the last b subsystems, the non-zero eigenvalues of the transposed moment operator are given by an explicit multinomial sum over pairs of compositions with fixed difference, and the rank equals the number of admissible difference vectors. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete eighty-line argument rather than an application of a known spectral theorem: it expands the toric Haar moment in the occupation basis, rewrites the partial transpose as a sum of rank-one operators indexed by the admissible difference vectors, constructs explicitly the eigenvectors attached to those vectors, and proves that the resulting family is orthogonal and that each member is non-zero, which simultaneously yields the eigenvalue formula and the rank. Combining the representation-theoretic structure of the partially transposed moment with the combinatorial bookkeeping of compositions of a fixed difference is research-level quantum information theory, beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
